title: The ether, the Far Horizon and the Void
summary: The outer reaches of the Umbra as mages know them.

claims.text: Etherships, mostly built by the Sons of Ether, cross the True Horizon; Technocratic faster-than-light tries in hyperspace always draw Paradox, so most Umbral craft fly near light speed.
The sea of ether ends at the Far Horizon, a barrier of hazards echoing the asteroid belt, whose once-charted paths are now chaotic.
Past it lies the Void, the Deep Umbra or Deep Universe, full of alien powers on which human belief has no hold.

title: Readings of the Avatar Storm
summary: How different mages explain the Storm.

claims.text: Some argue the Storm lashed back at mages who crowded the Near Umbra with vain Horizon Realms and drained Earth of Quintessence.
Many Marauders read it as the return of chaos, tearing apart all that was built in the Near Umbra.
The Avatar Storm always punishes mages who cross Earth's Gauntlet, while other dimensional barriers are free of it except for roving storms.

title: Shallowings
summary: Thin spots where the Gauntlet nearly vanished.

claims.text: Long ago the Gauntlet was far weaker, and the Order of Hermes named the spots where it almost failed Shallowings.
They were dangerous for what came through and prized because even mages poor at spirit magic could cross.
Human fear, apathy and disbelief have since thickened the Gauntlet until Shallowings are nearly gone, though a few open at certain times.

title: Crossing the Gauntlet
summary: Rules for stepping into the Otherworlds.

claims.text: Any barrier between dimensions is a pericarp; Earth's is the one written with a capital G.
Most barriers yield to Spirit 3 and Stepping Sideways: roll Arete against the Gauntlet's strength, with successes setting how long the crossing takes.
A botch can trap the mage or send the mage somewhere worse, such as a Zone.

title: The Penumbra
summary: The spirit shadow closest to Earth.

claims.text: Dreams, daydreams and odd minds can brush the Periphery, and mages can glimpse it on purpose with Mind or Spirit.
The Penumbra keeps roughly earthly space and distance, so Penumbral London sits across a Penumbral Channel from Penumbral France, all under a moonlit twilight.
It has three aspects matching the three layers of Realms within the Horizon; most travellers land in the Astral Penumbra by default.

title: The Alder Bole
summary: The World Tree that links every Umbra.

claims.text: The Alder Bole, also called Mount Qaf, runs through all Umbrae: its crown among the Astral Realms, its trunk in the Middle Umbra and its roots in the Low Umbra.
It is hard to find, but once reached, moving between layers is easy if one does not care where one ends up.
Since the Reckoning and the Storm, gateways and guides to the Afterworlds have become rare, and many doors to the Middle Umbra are one-way.

title: Shard Realms
summary: Worlds that mirror the sun, moon and planets.

claims.text: Each Shard Realm reflects a body of the solar system and is ruled by one of the Nine Spheres, making that Sphere's magic easier and often coincidental there.
Shard Realms were once reached through Shade Realms on the Horizon, but since the Storm those portals have turned treacherous or misleading.
Crossing the First Horizon needs Spirit 5, and some vanished Masters and Oracles are said to linger beyond it as ephemeral beings.
